summary: MATERIAL ROLE UPDATE / REPRICE REQUIRED: Baltimore officially downgraded Zay Flowers from doubtful to OUT at 16:18 ET Saturday. The Ravens explicitly state Rashod Bateman will move into the top receiver spot, with LaJohntay Wester, Devontez Walker, Chris Moore and Elijah Sarratt seeing more opportunity. This materially strengthens Bateman/Mark Andrews opportunity expectations, but PRIME is NOT promoting a bet from stale prices. The accessible CLEATZ receiving board is timestamped 13:49 ET, before Flowers was officially ruled out; it showed Bateman receiving yards O36.5 -111 DraftKings and receptions O2.5 -130 BetMGM, while Mark Andrews receiving yards was 48.5 +102 Pinnacle. Those quotes predate the catalyst and therefore are market-history context, not current executable sportsbook truth. Bateman ran a team-high 26 routes in Week 1 but earned only one target and zero catches; FantasyPros' 2025 profile also showed only a 10.5% target share, 0.76 YPRR and 10.9% first-read share. Stats Insider's current Week 2 model has Bateman at 42 receiving yards, but that projection alone cannot justify an Over. Andrews' Week 1 role was materially stronger (70% route share, 24% target share, 2.33 YPRR, 26.3% first-read share, one red-zone target); however, numberFire projects 38.3 receiving yards while Stats Insider projects 48, and the accessible 48.5 market already sits at/above those projections. Result: Bateman receiving yards/receptions WATCH and REPRICE_REQUIRED; Andrews receiving yards PASS/REPRICE_REQUIRED at a 48.5-type threshold. Do not use the pre-OUT 36.5/-111, 2.5/-130 or 48.5/+102 quotes as current. No new Grok pass. Existing Schultz/Taylor/Downs/Juwan/Dowdle/Rodgers states are unchanged from the 18:06 ET archive unless a fresh post-news book quote is later verified.

confirmedFacts.claim: Zay Flowers (hamstring) was downgraded from doubtful to OUT for Week 2 vs. New Orleans. Baltimore states Rashod Bateman will move into the top receiver spot, with LaJohntay Wester, Devontez Walker, Chris Moore and Elijah Sarratt seeing more opportunities.
Ja'Kobi Lane is on injured reserve following wrist surgery, further thinning Baltimore's wide-receiver room.
